analyst_view.overall: Sporting (8th, 23 pts, only 16 goals scored) host Las Palmas (11th, 20 pts), who won four in a row before losing 1-0 at Granada; Las Palmas have not lost to Sporting in the last six meetings. Sporting, under Nicolás Larcamón, have an injury crisis: besides Otero (second game of his ban) and Corredera (appeal rejected, banned), Gelabert (meniscus, out several weeks), Konrad and Pablo García are injured on top of Casas and Manu Rodríguez; the numbers list Otero, Corredera, Sarco, Manu Rodríguez and Casas but not Gelabert, Konrad or Pablo García, while Sarco, whom the numbers treat as out, returned to group training on Wednesday and may make the squad. Las Palmas miss Opoku (one-match ban, counted) and forward Sandro Ramírez (calf micro-tear, not in the numbers), but get Pezzolesi and Herzog back from the U21s. No referee named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and already take a lot off Sporting for Otero, Corredera, Sarco and Casas. They don't know that Gelabert, called a 'jugador diferencial' by Larcamón, plus Konrad and Pablo García are also out, nor that Las Palmas lose Sandro Ramírez; against that, Sarco is back training and may play. Net a small cut to about 2.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, with both sides' recent corner counts close to normal (+2% and +1% momentum). Sporting lose wide players Konrad and Pablo García, but Las Palmas' full-backs Pezzolesi and Andrés Rodríguez return to a settled back four that pushes on; nothing clearly shifts the count, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards and already add both teams' heavy recent booking (+9% Sporting, +13% Las Palmas); Sporting have had two reds in two games (Otero's confrontation with the referee, Corredera's double yellow) and Opoku was sent off after 104 seconds at Granada. That trend is what momentum captures and no referee is named, so I stay at 5.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots, boosted by Sporting's high recent shot count (+12%). With Gelabert, Konrad and Pablo García out on top of the listed absences, Sporting's attack relies on young Enol Prendes and a thin front line, so I trim slightly to about 24.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. Sporting are missing their most creative midfielder Gelabert (not in the numbers) and Las Palmas lose forward Sandro Ramírez for two to three weeks, so I shade down slightly to about 8.1.
